close_reason: Fixed in b9d8808. Four sites in memory.rs (Mailbox filter, Email filter, Email sort, EmailSubmission filter) now use .expect() pairs with documented infallibility rationale matching Pattern G (bc79c70). Added four serde-roundtrip probe tests in tests/integration.rs covering MailboxFilterCondition, EmailFilter (Condition + Operator variants), EmailSubmissionFilter, and Vec<EmailComparator> — these defend the .expect() claim against future serde-symmetry breaks. 247 integration tests pass; clippy clean.
description:
src/memory.rs lines 650-654 (mailbox), 685-690 (email), 706-711 (submission) all use:

  let typed_filter = filter.and_then(|f| serde_json::to_value(f).ok().and_then(|v| serde_json::from_value(v).ok()));

The .ok().and_then(.ok()) chain silently drops the filter on either serde_json::to_value failure or from_value failure. Result: a request with a filter the backend cannot decode is processed as if no filter was supplied — returning ALL objects when the client expected a filtered subset. This is a correctness bug masquerading as a no-op.

In practice both ends are derive-Serialize/Deserialize on the same type, so the roundtrip should be infallible. But the bc79c70 (Pattern G) policy is explicit that 'infallible' must use .expect() with a stated reason, not .ok() fallback. If a future field on EmailFilterCondition adds custom serialization that's lossy, the silent drop turns into a silent correctness bug with no signal. Fix: replace each .ok().and_then(.ok()) pair with two .expect() calls and a comment citing why infallibility holds.
title: Pattern G regression: memory.rs filter roundtrip silently drops malformed filters
